data.title: AI Drives Flood of Crypto Bug Reports as Platforms Expand Automated Triage
data.description:
Crypto bug bounty platforms are using artificial intelligence to manage a surge in security reports, as AI tools help researchers find vulnerabilities while also generating more invalid and duplicate submissions. According to Cointelegraph, HackenProof said in October that AI was triaging 70% of its submissions fully autonomously, with a goal of reaching 85% by the end of 2026. The platform received an average of about 6,100 reports per month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the volume recorded in December last year. Rival Immunefi said last week that submissions increased 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, and introduced a tool to flag duplicate reports before submission. Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to identify and report potential security flaws, but the growing volume is making it harder for security teams to prioritize urgent threats. Bron founder Dmitry Tokarev said teams that have not adopted AI for sorting reports are like “bringing a sword to a gunfight.” Several platforms marked February as a turning point, coinciding with the release of more capable AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6. HackenProof said the model can handle larger codebases and longer tasks, while HackerOne described a shift away from a “human-only submission environment.”

Crypto developers are also testing measures to discourage low-quality reports. In October, the team behind Firedancer, a Solana validator client developed by Jump Crypto, began requiring researchers to burn 1 SOL for each report they want considered for a bounty; the token is destroyed even if the submission is a duplicate. The team also uses AI to screen reports. In a November update published Tuesday, HackerOne vice president of operations Tony Lee said the company began requiring identity verification before submissions in the third quarter, expanded its triage team and started using AI agents to automatically close clear-cut spam and duplicate cases. In October, it also gave customers more control over the volume of reports received by public programs. Lee said he expects reports to keep rising “for the foreseeable future,” after volume increased 22% in Q3 from the previous quarter. On Wednesday, insurer QBE and risk consultancy Control Risks forecast more disruptive cyber incidents in 2027 across the 14 markets they studied, citing the “industrialization of AI” as a factor. Mike Blank, chief product officer at R3, said he expects hacks to rise sharply in 2027, while urging crypto teams to focus on the potential damage from a breach. He said the key difference will be whether a stolen key can drain a protocol’s assets or only pause operations.

data.title: Seraphim Says Abraxas Capital Exited Hyperliquid Over Limited Profit Potential at Its Scale
data.description: Crypto trader and former Ethena Labs growth lead Seraphim said Abraxas Capital exited Hyperliquid because its capital scale left too little room for profit. According to Odaily, the hedge fund recently closed all its positions on Hyperliquid and withdrew its remaining funds. Seraphim said he knew the Abraxas team, including its founder, and that its operations were much larger than many might expect; DeFi and most centralized exchanges were too small for the firm, whose focus was entirely on investment returns.

data.title: Address Suspected of Accumulating 8,000 ETH Three Hours Ago
data.description: An address was suspected of accumulating 8,000 ETH three hours ago. According to Foresight News, monitoring by @ai_9684xtpa found that the address deposited 7,346.7 ETH to an exchange four months ago at $1,788.7 per ETH.

data.title: Japan Adds eTakara to List of Unregistered Financial Dealers
data.description:
Japan’s Financial Services Agency updated its list of unregistered financial dealers on November 26, adding several companies, including Japanese firm eTakara.

According to Odaily, the companies are suspected of soliciting over-the-counter derivatives trades online without registration. eTakara’s website says it offers stock, foreign exchange and crypto asset trading, and that users receive a self-custody wallet upon registration. Its customer agreement describes crypto asset contracts for difference and says accounts support leverage of up to 400 times. The Kanto Local Finance Bureau said foreign exchange margin trading and margin trading using crypto assets must be registered under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act.

data.title: Japan's Financial Services Agency Considers Cooling-Off Period for Transfers From Newly Opened Exchange Accounts
data.description: Japan's Financial Services Agency is considering requiring crypto exchanges to impose a cooling-off period on transfers to self-custody wallets from newly opened accounts. According to Foresight News, the proposal aims to address fraud and money-laundering risks involving exchanges and self-custody wallets. The document is not a final rule, and regulators are seeking public comment on whether to require transfer delays or display a warning before transactions.

data.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam Upgrade Set for Hoodi Testnet Activation on December 15, 2026
data.description:
Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled to activate on the Hoodi testnet at 19:12 UTC on December 15, 2026, at epoch 143,616. According to Odaily, core developers reached several agreements at their 192nd All Core Developers Consensus meeting on November 26, including proceeding on the basis that execution-layer teams broadly agreed to keep the current EIP-8037 specification unchanged. Developers also finalized the upgrade’s execution payload validation mechanism.

For the Hegotá upgrade, FOCIL will temporarily remain a key consensus-layer feature, though debate has reopened and developers will continue evaluating it at future meetings. They also discussed post-quantum security proposals, including using Keccak-256 as a hash function, but made no final decision. Glamsterdam’s mainnet activation date has not been set, and client teams expect to release versions for the Hoodi testnet upgrade early next week.

data.title: Sequent Raises $2.2 Million in Pre-Seed Round Led by Frachtis and Metaplanet
data.description: Sequent has raised $2.2 million in a pre-seed round co-led by Frachtis and Metaplanet, with Curve as its first paying customer. According to Odaily, Sequent’s product Alan is a formal verification tool that lets users state security rules in natural language. Alan uses AI to convert the rules into mathematical form and automatically search for mathematical proofs, which are then checked by HOL4, an independent checker that does not use AI. The funding will support Alan’s full launch and expand support for languages including Solidity, Solana and Rust.

data.title: Trump Says Wednesday’s Sharp Wall Street Selloff Briefly Worried Him
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, U.S. President Donald Trump said Wednesday’s sharp stock-market decline briefly worried him, though major indexes recovered most of their losses. He told reporters that seeing some substantial declines the previous day had concerned him, but stocks had risen again by the close.

The Nasdaq fell more than 4% at one point Wednesday before rebounding to finish slightly lower. Trump also said markets reacted positively to Jensen Huang resuming as Nvidia’s CEO, adding that the market felt good about it.

data.title: South Korea’s Presidential Office Convenes Emergency Meeting to Strengthen Anti-Hacking Measures
data.description:
South Korea’s presidential office convened an emergency meeting with financial regulators to strengthen defenses against hacking and prevent further losses. According to Odaily, the National Security Office said the meeting was chaired by its Third Deputy Director, Song Ki-ho, and attended by the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Financial Security Institute.

The Financial Services Commission presented measures to prevent further losses, including the use of an abnormal transaction detection system (FDS) and an AI-based voice phishing detection system. Song called on regulators to strengthen two-factor authentication, including one-time password (OTP) generators, and incorporate AI into the FDS. The National Security Office said it would also step up blocking and investigations of websites illegally selling leaked information.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Wallet Replay Mechanism Linked Addresses to Node IPs in 30 Successful Simulations
data.description:
Researchers found that a deterministic signal in Bitcoin Core wallet transaction replays can link an on-chain address to the IP address of a node running the wallet. According to Odaily, after an attacker sends a low-fee transaction to a confirmed address, a wallet holding that address periodically rebroadcasts it during a 12-to-36-hour replay window; monitoring P2P transaction announcements from candidate nodes can identify the associated node. The method also applies to hot and watch-only wallets because they check script membership without verifying private keys.

In regtest simulations, researchers tested five target wallets over six rounds and successfully linked the addresses to the correct nodes in all 30 attribution attempts. They estimated the cost of an implanted transaction at $0.18 to $0.34, based on a Bitcoin price of about $59,000 on November 25, 2026.

The -privatebroadcast setting does not prevent the leak: if a transaction remains unconfirmed beyond the 12-to-36-hour window, periodic replays revert to broadcasting to all peers. Nodes operating on multiple networks replay transactions across those networks; only nodes configured solely with -onlynet=onion can avoid exposing a clearnet IP address. Affected software includes Bitcoin Core, Bitcoin Knots, Sparrow in core mode, Specter Desktop, Liana, Fully Noded, Gordian Wallet, JoinMarket, Jam, Lily Wallet, Electrum Personal Server, Caravan, bwt and Eclair.

Setting -walletbroadcast=0 disables all wallet broadcasts, including the initial broadcast of new transactions; users must relay them manually with sendrawtransaction. Bitcoin Core PR 36482 proposes replaying only transactions newly added to the mempool to remove the planted-transaction signal, but it has not been released. Researchers ismaelsadeeq and polespinasa jointly conceived the study during Bitcoin Research Week, and the simulation code is available on GitHub. They noted that node identity does not establish common ownership: one entity may operate multiple nodes, and a watch-only wallet may track addresses it does not own.

data.title: Scammers Use Frozen USDT to Lure TRON Users and Steal TRX Deposits
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Crypto Briefing, scammers on the TRON network are using USDT frozen by Tether as bait, directing victims to wallets showing large USDT balances and asking them to send TRX to cover supposed unlocking or transfer fees. Once the TRX arrives, automated bots typically sweep it away within about 1.1 minutes, while the frozen USDT remains immovable.

FreezeCheck has flagged multiple trap wallets using this scheme. At least seven are linked to more than $2.54 million in frozen USDT, which represents the scale of the bait, not victims’ losses.

As of mid-November 2026, Tether’s blacklist included more than 8,361 TRON addresses where USDT transfers were blocked but TRX deposits could still be received. Tether, TRON, and Chainalysis formed a digital crime task force on November 12 to combat illicit USDT activity on the TRON network.

data.title: Curve Fees Rise About 50% to $5.6 Million Over 30 Days
data.description:
Curve Finance’s fee revenue increased about 50% to $5.6 million over the past 30 days. According to Odaily, DefiLlama Research data showed trading volume nearly doubled to $4.8 billion during the same period. Liquidity providers received $3.7 million in fees, up 107%, and their share of total fees rose from 47% to 66%.

Curve’s own revenue, including bribe income, was $1.9 million, down 2%. It remained broadly unchanged despite the near doubling in trading volume.

data.title: AI TRENDS | DeepSeek Tests Chat-Cost Display After Introducing Usage Limits
data.description: Some DeepSeek users report that the company is testing a feature on its website and mobile app to show the amount consumed in each conversation. According to Odaily, after a conversation, the interface displays the number of tokens used and an estimated cost based on API pricing. DeepSeek’s chat service for individual users remains free, while the feature makes the computing cost of each conversation visible.

data.title: Paul Tudor Jones’ Fund Raises IBIT Holdings 98% to $64.6 Million
data.description:
Paul Tudor Jones’ macro fund, Tudor Investment Corporation, increased its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) by 98% in the third quarter of 2026, to about $64.6 million.

According to Odaily, a 13F filing submitted to the SEC on November 16 showed the fund held 1,363,567 IBIT shares as of September 30, up 675,038 shares from 688,529 at the end of the second quarter. The earlier position was valued at $22.9 million.

data.title: Dollar Set for Longest Monthly Winning Streak in Two Years
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bloomberg, the U.S. dollar is on track for its longest run of monthly gains in two years, Bloomberg reported on November 26. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 1.8% in November and is poised to advance for a third consecutive month.

The dollar has strengthened against all Group of 10 currencies, including the Japanese yen and Swiss franc. The rally, driven by the unwinding of AI-related trades and rising interest rates that boosted demand for safe-haven assets, would mark the longest monthly winning streak since 2024.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Contributor Reveals Wallet-to-IP Link Can Cost Under $0.35
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CoinDesk, Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail said in a November 25 post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum that Bitcoin Core wallets automatically rebroadcast transactions after they remain unconfirmed for about 12 to 36 hours. The behavior could be used to link monitored Bitcoin addresses to the IP addresses of the nodes associated with them.

Ismail conducted 30 tests on a test network running standard Bitcoin Core and identified the correct node in all 30. The method has not yet been measured on Bitcoin’s mainnet. Based on a Bitcoin price of about $60,000, each attempt costs an estimated $0.18 to $0.34, or less than $0.35.

The issue affects Bitcoin Core hot wallets and watch-only wallets, as well as Sparrow in Core mode, Specter, Liana, JoinMarket and Electrum Personal Server. Nodes using Tor while retaining a clearnet connection may still expose their real IP addresses when rebroadcasting. Using only the onion network or disabling wallet broadcasts can limit exposure. Funds and private keys are not affected, according to the report.

A code-change proposal, PR #36482, has not been released. Bitcoin Core contributor Martin Zumsande said the proposal would only modestly increase the cost of the method and recommended making rebroadcasts after receipt of a payment an opt-in feature.

data.title: Mike Howell: Bitcoin to Be Top Allocation Asset as Financial Liquidity Returns
data.description:
CrossBorder Capital founder Mike Howell recommends that investors gradually allocate to gold, silver and Bitcoin with a two-year investment horizon rather than focus on short-term returns. According to Odaily, Howell says that when the global real economy cools, U.S. Treasury yields fall and liquidity flows back into the financial system, markets will reach a turning point, with Bitcoin as the preferred allocation asset, followed by gold and silver.

Howell says the global liquidity cycle, which measures the availability of credit and capital, peaked at the end of 2025. He says financial markets are unlikely to move against the cycle and have probably entered a bear market, with difficult conditions for stocks potentially lasting through the end of the first half of 2027. Early signs of the liquidity peak appeared early this year, when Bitcoin, the asset most sensitive to global liquidity, peaked near $125,000. Gold and silver weakened afterward, and bond and stock markets also came under pressure from tighter liquidity. Howell says heavy capital spending in AI, expansion of the real economy, corporate bond issuance by large technology companies and fundraising for mega IPOs are creating substantial demand for capital markets.

data.title: South Korea Considers Expanding Stock Market Stabilization Fund
data.description:
South Korea is reviewing an expansion of its stock market stabilization fund and procedures for activating it during periods of increased market volatility. According to Odaily, Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il will meet Friday with Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song, Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon and Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin to discuss procedures related to the fund.

A Finance Ministry official said verifying the activation procedures is the current priority and that no decision has been made on whether to use the fund under current conditions. Financial authorities are considering increasing its size beyond the 10.76 trillion won already committed. Lee previously said the fund’s size would be reviewed based on circumstances when it is activated.

data.title: Flop Labs Opens FLOP Testnet Miner Access, With More Than 50 Miners Online
data.description: Flop Labs has opened miner access to the FLOP testnet. According to Odaily, more than 50 miners are online, using GPUs including the RTX 3090, H200 and B300; the devices have completed on-chain calibration and are available to provide services. The project has invited more GPU owners to join the testnet.

data.title: Trump Says Jensen Huang Is “Fine,” Citing Information He Has
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Jensen Huang was “fine,” citing information in his possession, after a reporter asked how he could determine Huang posed no security threat when the Justice Department had not conducted an appropriate investigation. According to Odaily, the reporter asked what information Trump was relying on, and Trump replied that he had a lot of information.
